_note: Closed variety of scripts/stand_access.py (FR-13, AR-1, OH3-10): the shapes in which a stand's 400/422 answer to the login call names the body fields it complains about. One reader: stand_access.complained_fields(). A shape is {kind, ...}: kind `list_item_path` = the answer's top-level `list` key holds a list, and each item holds the field name at `name_at` (a path of object keys; a string there is the name, a list there yields its LAST string, so FastAPI's loc ["body", "email"] names `email`); kind `key_names` = the answer's top-level `map` key holds an object whose KEYS are the field names (a Laravel/Django-style {"errors": {"email": [...]}}). Only NAMES come out: a candidate must match `name_pattern`, is dropped when it is one of `not_fields` (the places of a field, not a field) or contains a credential the call used, and at most `max_names` are kept. Nothing else of the answer is ever read out. A shape this table does not hold names nothing, and the receipt says only the status.
